methods.label: Count the possible integer outputs
methods.explanation:
For both square roots to be real, we need \(x\ge0\) and \(\sqrt{x}\le120\), or \(0\le x\le14400\).

Let
\[
n=\sqrt{120-\sqrt{x}}
\]
be an integer. A principal square root is nonnegative, so \(n\ge0\). Squaring gives
\[
n^2=120-\sqrt{x},
\]
which implies \(n^2\le120\). Since \(10^2=100\le120<121=11^2\), the only possible integer outputs are
\[
n=0,1,2,\ldots,10.
\]
For each of these, rearranging gives \(\sqrt{x}=120-n^2\), so there is exactly one possible input:
\[
x=(120-n^2)^2.
\]
These inputs all work. Indeed, \(120-n^2\ge20>0\), so their inner square root equals \(120-n^2\), and the outer square root equals \(\sqrt{n^2}=n\).

Different nonnegative integers \(n\) have different squares, hence different values of \(\sqrt{x}=120-n^2\) and therefore different inputs \(x\). Thus the eleven outputs correspond to eleven distinct valid real inputs. The answer is \(\boxed{11}\), choice E.
